texto: Static locked-off tripod shot, camera does not move, stable frame, only the subject moves.
Slow smooth dolly in toward the subject, steady forward push on rails, framing tightens from medium shot to close-up, no shake.
Slow smooth dolly out away from the subject, steady backward pull revealing more of the environment, no shake.
Smooth lateral dolly moving left, camera slides sideways parallel to the subject, background parallax, steady and level.
Smooth lateral dolly moving right, camera slides sideways parallel to the subject, background parallax, steady and level.
Fast, long continuous dolly in from a wide shot all the way to an extreme close-up of the subject's eyes, fluid and stabilized.
Fast, long continuous dolly out from a close-up of the subject to a wide establishing shot, fluid and stabilized.
Dolly zoom vertigo effect: camera dollies in while the lens zooms out, subject stays the same size while the background stretches and warps.
Crash zoom in: sudden very fast zoom punching into the subject's face, snaps and holds, crisp, no camera shake after the stop.
Crash zoom out: sudden very fast zoom pulling back from close-up to wide, snaps and holds steady.
Slow gradual optical zoom in, camera position fixed, tension builds as the frame tightens on the subject.
Yo-yo zoom: quick zoom in then immediately back out on the beat, rhythmic punch, stable camera body.
Smooth 360-degree orbit around the subject at eye level, constant speed, subject stays centered and in focus.
Slow arc shot curving counterclockwise around the subject, about 90 degrees, subject centered, smooth gimbal motion.
Slow arc shot curving clockwise around the subject, about 90 degrees, subject centered, smooth gimbal motion.
Bullet time: action frozen in extreme slow motion while the camera sweeps in a fast semicircle around the subject, particles suspended in the air.
Crane up: camera rises vertically from ground level to a high angle, revealing the scene below, smooth and stable.
Crane down: camera descends from a high angle down to the subject's eye level, smooth and stable.
Overhead top-down bird's-eye shot, camera looking straight down at the subject, slow gentle rotation.
FPV drone shot: fast agile first-person drone flight, diving and weaving through the environment, banking smoothly around obstacles, horizon stable.
Aerial pullback: drone starts close on the subject and flies backward and upward, revealing a vast landscape or city.
Helicopter aerial shot: high wide view gliding slowly over the city, smooth long lateral movement, stable horizon.
Tracking shot: camera follows the subject from behind at shoulder height as they walk, smooth steadicam glide.
Leading tracking shot: camera moves backward in front of the subject as they walk toward it, steadicam, face stays in frame.
Subtle handheld camera with gentle natural breathing motion, documentary feel, no violent shake, no jitter.
Snorricam: camera rigidly mounted to the subject's body, their face stays locked in the center of frame while the world moves around them.
Slow smooth pan left from a fixed position, horizontal rotation revealing the scene.
Slow smooth pan right from a fixed position, horizontal rotation revealing the scene.
Whip pan: extremely fast horizontal pan with motion blur used as a transition to the next shot, lands clean and steady.
Slow tilt up from the subject's feet to the face, camera fixed in place, reveal from bottom to top.
Slow tilt down from the sky or skyline to the subject, camera fixed in place.
Dutch angle: camera tilted 20 degrees off horizontal, uneasy dynamic composition, slow push in.
Fisheye lens close to the subject, strong barrel distortion, low angle, skate-video energy, smooth movement.
Hero shot: low angle looking up at the subject, slow push in and slight rise, subject looks powerful against the sky.
Robotic arm motion-control move: precise fast sweeping move that stops exactly on the subject, mechanical smoothness, commercial look.
Camera moves forward through a gap, window or doorway, passing through the object into the next space without a cut.
Rack focus: focus shifts from the foreground object to the subject in the background, shallow depth of field, camera static.
Hyperlapse: camera moves forward through the city while time is sped up, people and traffic streak past, stabilized.
Low shutter speed look: subject sharp while lights and movement leave soft motion-blur trails, dreamy smear, stable camera.
Car chase camera: low tracking shot alongside the moving car at speed, road blur, smooth stabilized rig.
